messages:
Noah (Product): quick sync: prototyped the sticky approval rail for Prompt Sets. it shows aggregated mini-metrics, a compact regression heatmap edge, and the bulk approve action. dropping mock: https://figma.redwood/rail-mini-score

Lina (Design): cool. two immediate questions: 1) does the rail replace per-row affordances or complement them? 2) how do we show a very small scorecard inline without cluttering the run row?

Ethan (Eng): complement. plan: keep a subtle inline mini-score (2 numbers + status pill) and show the rail only after selection(s). technically the rail is trivial. challenge: touch behavior for inline quick-approve—hover won't work on mobile so we need a persistent small hit area or long-press.

Maya (Research): user notes: reviewers often want to "bookmark" borderline runs to revisit. can the rail include a pinned list or quick-access stack? also in our last study people missed the regression badge when it was purely color.

Ravi (Accessibility): a11y points: badges must not rely on color alone; include explicit text like "Regressions: 2" and ensure it's in the reading order. the rail needs keyboard focus order that doesn't trap users unexpectedly; provide a skip-to-rail link. toast messages (undo) should use role=alert and be concise.

Sam (Analytics): events to add: rail_open, approve_via_rail, approve_via_row, pin_run, blind_review_toggle. also capture input_mode (keyboard/mouse/touch). we'll want to segment by 'density setting' later.

Lina (Design): microcopy proposal: rail header "Selected: 3 — summary"; approve CTA "Approve selected"; pin CTA "Save for review"; mini-score labels "Q1: pass rate" and "Q2: regression count". tooltip for heatmap: "Regression density along runs".

Ethan (Eng): implementation notes: mini-score will be server-provided summary (cheap). heatmap edge is purely CSS gradient + aria-label for screen readers. pinning needs a small pinnedRuns API (append-only with order). long-press on mobile to reveal quick-approve could conflict with system long-press; safer to use a persistent 24px tap target.

Maya (Research): suggestion: add a 'blind-review' lab toggle in rail to hide user and prompt metadata for selected items. we ran a small test and it reduced identity bias on label tasks. keep it opt-in.

Ravi (Accessibility): blind-review must still expose necessary context via aria-describedby; don't remove alt text or role info. provide an obvious way to unblind and explain what fields are hidden. also keep contrast for the heatmap and badges at AA levels.

Noah (Product): product decision draft: adopt sticky rail + inline mini-score + persistent small tap target for mobile quick-approve + blind-review lab toggle + accessible textual badges + analytics events. would like Lina & Ethan to prototype rail + mobile behavior.

Lina (Design): will deliver desktop + mobile mocks. proposing the mini-score be left of run title (compact) and heatmap as a 6px left edge with a numeric badge on the right. also including focus outlines and keyboard skip link in mocks.

Ethan (Eng): I'll prototype rail and add a pinnedRuns endpoint. ETA: prototype branch in 9 days. I'll include a feature-flag for blind-review.

Sam (Analytics): I'll add the events to our schema and draft a dashboard to track approve_via_rail vs approve_via_row. recommend instrumenting time-to-approve metric to see if rail speeds up reviews.

Maya (Research): I'll run a quick internal task once prototype is ready: measure detection time for regressions with/without heatmap edge and with blind-review enabled. aiming for 50 internal raters.

Ravi (Accessibility): I'll produce an a11y acceptance checklist and run it on the prototype. quick list: skip-to-rail, aria-live toasts, textual badges, keyboard shortcuts w/ modifiers, focus-visible states.

Noah (Product): sounds good. final ask: Lina, include the 'undo' microcopy in mocks: toast text: "Runs approved — undo" and ensure it is announced. Ethan, make undo available for 7s by default.

deploy-bot: preview available at https://staging.redwood/prompt-sets/2334007890-rail-preview — please drop quick reactions or comments by EOD Friday.
